explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates LLM-based correctness judgments against human evaluation on 840 randomly sampled answers, reporting 98% agreement between human and LLM judgments.

prompts.notes: Prompt 2 in Appendix A.1 is used for LLM-based correctness checking, comparing answers to ground truth.

guidelines.notes: No specific human evaluation guidelines or rubric details provided beyond manual verification of correctness.

sample_size.notes: Validation was conducted on a randomly sampled subset of 840 answers out of the full 18,171 instances.

quantitative_scores.notes: Human judgment agrees with LLM-based metrics 98% of the time

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-based evaluation achieved 98% agreement with human judgments, demonstrating high reliability for automated correctness assessment using ChatGPT.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluation focused exclusively on correctness of factual answers, with humans validating the LLM's correctness judgments.
